summary: The root خَبَأ primarily means to hide or conceal something, making it unseen or unknown. It can also refer to something that is stored away or kept secret.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: خَبَأَهُ, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. خَبَاَ, (Msb, K,) inf. n. خَبْءٌ, (S, Msb,) He hid, or concealed, it; (Mgh, Msb, K;) as also, [but app. in an intensive sense, or applying to a number of things,] (K,) inf. n. تَخْبِئَةٌ; (TA;) and. (K.) He kept it, preserved it, guarded it, or took care of it. and he did so much; and well, or carefully. (Msb.) [ He laid it up; stored it, or reposited it, in a place of safety. ]
خَبَّاَ see 1, in two places. [Hence, خبّأ جَارِيَةً He kept a girl carefully concealed from view: see the pass. part. n., below.]
خَابَأْتُهُ مَا كَ َا, (K,) inf. n. مُخَابَأَةٌ, (TK,) I proposed to him as an enigma, What is such a thing? syn. حَاجَيْتُهُ. (K. [See also 8.])

اختبأ It was, or became, hidden, or concealed: (Mgh:) he hid, or concealed, himself. (S.) It is also trans.: see 1. [Hence,] اختبأ لَهُ He expressed a thing enigmatically to him, and then asked him respecting it. (IDrd, K. [See also 3.])

خَبْءٌ خبء (S, Msb, K) and (TA) and, of the measure فُعْلَةٌ from الخبأ [or rather الخَبْءُ ], like غُرْفَةٌ and قُبْضَةٌ from الغَرْفُ and القَبْضُ, (Har p. 426,) and (S, K) and, (K,) of which last the pl. is خَبَايَا, (TA,) A thing that is hidden, or concealed, (S, * Msb, K,) and absent, or unseen. (K.) [Hence,] خَبْءُ السَّمَآءِ The rain. (Th, S, K.) And خَبْءُ الأَرْضِ The plants, or herbage.
خِبْءٌ خبء: see the next preceding paragraph.

خَبْأَةٌ A daughter; syn. بِنْتٌ. (K, TA. [In the CK, النَّبْتُ is put for البِنْتُ.]) Hence the prov., خَبْأَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ يَفَعَةِ سَوْءٍ [ A daughter is better than a grown-up boy of evil deeds ]. (TA.) [In Freytag's Arab. Prov., i. 438, the first word in this prov. is written خُبَأَة, and followed by صِدْقٍ.] Aboo-Zeyd Sa'eed Ibn-Ows El-Ansáree entitled one of his books كتاب خبأة because he commenced it by mentioning خبأة in the sense of بنت, quoting the foregoing prov.
اِمْرَأَةٌ خُبَأَةٌ A woman who shows herself and then hides herself: (S, O, TA:) [like قُبَعَةٌ:] or a woman who keeps to her house, or tent. (K.)

خِبَآءٌ خبآء A well-known kind of structure; (K;) [i. e.] a kind of tent, (Mgh, TA,) made of wool, (Mgh, Msb,) or of camels' fur, or sometimes of [ goats' ] hair, sometimes upon two poles, or three; what is above this kind being termed بَيْتٌ: (Msb:) or a tent having one pole; that which has more than one pole being termed بيت: (AZ, TA in art. ربع:) [or] also applied to a بيت [or tent ] of any kind: (Towsheeh, TA voce بَيْتٌ, q. v.:) pl.
خَبِىْءٌ خبىء خبيء خبئ: see خَبْءٌ: and see also 8.
خَبِيْئَةٌ, and its pl. خَبَايَا: see خَبٌءٌ, in two places.
كَيْدٌ خَابِئٌ An artifice, or a stratagem, resulting in disappointment; i. q. خَائِبٌ; (AHei, K;) formed [from the latter] by transposition. (AHei.)

خَابِئَةٌ, as sometimes pronounced, (Msb,) or خَابِيَةٌ, with the ء suppressed, (S, Msb, K,) because of frequent usage, (Msb,) i. q. حُبٌّ [q. v.]; (S, K;) i. e. A large jar: pl. خوابى [i. e. خَوَابِئُ, or خَوَابٍ ]: (TA:) from خَبَأَهُ “ he hid it, ” or “ concealed it. ” (S, Msb.) [Hence,] بِنْتُ الخَابِيَةِ (assumed tropical:) Wine. (Har p. 365.)
مَخْبَأٌ A place, or chamber, for hiding or concealing [ anything ]; a secret place or chamber: pl. مَخَابِئُ. (MA.)

جَارِيَةٌ مُخَبَّأَةٌ; so in the [S and] O, and in some of the correct copies of the K; in other copies of the K مُخْبَأَةٌ; (TA;) [and thus in the CK;] A girl that is [ kept in the house, or tent, ] concealed from view; or that conceals herself; (S;) that is kept behind, or within, the curtain; (K, TA;) not going forth: or (TA) that is not yet married. (Lth, K, TA.)
مُخْتَبِئٌ One who conceals himself in order that he may see without the knowledge of him who is seen. (Mgh.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
